about: Curated list of crossing devices for requirement R4. Replaces the keyword role "crossing" of build_graph.py. Generated by curated/mk_devices.py; edit that file.

states.floored: yields a proved statement about zeros with a floor above 1/2 fixed by the method
states.open: not closed by any row or lane; may be under test in a running lane

devices.name: Coherent set with large sieve (7/8 type): the only mechanism meeting R1-R3

devices.name: Effective order 2 in the 7/8 architecture (h = r/2): closed as an attack lead after round 10
devices.evidence: map section 6 item 1; narrowed after round 6 (lesson 1) to derivation items. Closed parts: re-expression of the same probe (Lemma U, two referees; row Z15b); abelian families (row Z22; abstract-family statement ARGUED); double covers through local data (row Z23, claim narrowed by its referee); probes of higher degree in the target (row Z15c); long marks at h = 3 as an input weaker than GRH (row Z26); the sextic probe as a route below abscissa 2/3 (normaliser H_eta, row Z24, two referees). Left open: (a) the uncompensated high side derived from manuscript (12.5)/(16.1) with the normaliser kept; (b) the compensated principal signal below Re s = 3/5; (c) whether any model vertex with 1 < h <= 3 exists. Requirement added: the normaliser of the probe has no zeros in Re s > 1/2. State set to closed by the strategy review after round 10 (STRATEGY v3, section 3.1 item 22): items (a) to (c) were derived in rounds 7 to 10 and each ends at an input of zero-free type for the twist family of the target or fails in the F_q[T] model ((E-K) row Z30, (E-H) row Z31, normaliser ladder rows Z24, Z24b, Hilbert-Schmidt cap, completed rows at (6, 9, 2)). Several closures are measured or argued, not theorems. Reopen only with one of: a relation among the reciprocals 1/L across rows that is not a norm bound; a method keeping the signs of the dual sum in the window Z/P < X < ZP; a probe whose normaliser has no zeros in Re s > 1/2; global Whittaker constants of a genuine cusp form on the double cover of GL(3)

devices.name: Sections of the prime chain on a Reinhardt (Laurent) shell around the critical torus, gamma one-port included
devices.evidence: lane c7-laurent-shell-gamma-section (round 7, one referee): the first-moment bracket has no forced sign for zeta or for DH on the shell or with the gamma term; every statement holds for DH; the limit step is void in measure form and is the height-coupled reserve inequality of g-passive-cascade in formula form. Map rows under Q12/Q22 owed. Not covered: a section with P(t) growing like a power of t

devices.name: Prop. 2.1 probe with signal constant h > 1 in F_q[T] (region lx < l), where the Riemann hypothesis is a theorem
devices.evidence: lane c7-ff-order2-vertex-exact (round 7, one referee; q = 7, 13, N <= 4): base probe at lx < l re-expresses blocks with h < 1; the uncompensated marked probe has h > 1 where RH holds, but its low input (diagonal-level row bound) contains the squared signal and fails for the Moebius-twisted weight. Round 8 (c8-ek-ff-reflected-rows-exact, one referee): compensated probe (12.5) computed at dual length 0: h > 1 survives, the rescaled term is about q^(-lam) of the marked signal, the low input is unchanged. Left open: reflected completed rows; threshold test undecided at N <= 4. Constraint from row Z24: the normaliser must have no zeros in Re s > 1/2. State set to closed as a crossing device by the strategy review after round 10 (STRATEGY v3, section 3.1 item 23): c9-mv6-ff-window-exact (exact, pre-registered: the diagonal-level row bound fails in active classes at N = 2 above dual length 3N), c10-ff-completed-rows-692 (run (6, 9, 2), q = 7: completed energy 1.69 to 5.9 times the diagonal; the completed-row law fails with exact inputs; one configuration, no exponent), c10-ff-slot-cross-decomposition (the excess is a cross term over pairs of marked primes and is not target-specific: random multiplicative signs are not separated, 50 of 51), c10-ff-signal-intersection-square (the squared signal is an intersection square for an algebraic reason in genus 1 and holds for fakes with off-line zeros). One referee each. Kept as a bounded model question with no requirement flag: whether the non-principal half of the cube term is bounded once the principal signal is removed; genus >= 2 targets. Reopen as a device only with a low input that does not contain the squared signal

devices.name: (E-K): mean square of reflected marked theta rows for the probe vector itself, dual longer than the row set
devices.evidence: named by c7-probe-format-h-cap (one referee; second referee of Theorem K and Lemma A in push/c8-repair-engine-map-r7/c7-probe-format-h-cap/REFEREE2.md). Not an operator-norm statement: every blockwise l2-l2 estimate of the reflected rows is at or above the K-branch (Hilbert-Schmidt). Under test in round 8 (c8-ek-ff-reflected-rows-exact, c8-ek-theta-second-moment-formula). Model value with the polar term kept: 31/36, no vertex with h > 1 (first referee E2); form of the hypothesis corrected by first referee E3. Ceiling 2/3 from row Z24. Round 8 (state kept open, narrowed; one referee each): c8-ek-theta-second-moment-formula: the row mean square equals X D + X Sum_k F_k exactly, F_k bilinear in Moebius sums over the order-6 twist family of the target, so (E-K) is a mean value of 1/L over a family containing the target (zero-free type; holds for X >= ZP under GRH for the family, outline only); c8-ek-ff-reflected-rows-exact: in F_q[T] row energy = diagonal + squared signal, targets not separated from random vectors (reflected completed rows not run). Left open after round 8: the window Z/P < X < ZP. Round 9 (planner edit, round 10; c9-mv6-window-statement, c9-mv6-ff-window-exact, one referee each; evidence text corrected against the two referee files by c10-repair-record-referee-r9): closed for two named absolute-value techniques (family GRH pointwise; the second-moment step of c8-liou-row-bound-theorem): the 1/L form with more dual frequencies than columns has its own diagonal and both techniques return N^(1+eps); this is ARGUED + MEASURED, no lower bound is proved for the Moebius vector, and a method that keeps the signs of the dual sum or works on the row side is not excluded (referee E1). In F_q[T] at N = 2 (exact integers, rule pre-registered: FAILS) the probe vectors of quadratic Weil targets have row energy 1.19 to 20.6 (q = 7) and 2.17 to 18.1 (q = 13) times the diagonal in active classes with sharp degree classes, rising in steps (two at q = 7, one at q = 13), not a fitted exponent; in inactive classes they are below the diagonal; a bound restricted to inactive classes or with weights removing the sixth-power frequencies is not tested; reflected dual sums not built; N = 3 undecided (referee E1 to E6). Model excess and the Z[omega] screen (ratio at most 1.007) not reconciled. Map row Z30. Outstanding bounded check: completed rows, run (6, 9, 2) at q = 7

devices.name: (E-H): cancellation over non-principal rows below the floor-class high bound
devices.evidence: named by c7-probe-format-h-cap; values corrected by its referee (E1: 4/5 with G = 0, 13/15 with the polar term kept, 1 - 2/r only in the three-input model). Round 8, c8-eh-nonprincipal-row-cancellation (state kept open: the referee does not hold the circularity headline): NP = I - I_1 exactly, so a bound on NP is necessary and sufficient for the conclusion given the low estimate (necessity, not circularity); termwise and norm treatments closed in the model (13/15; 31/36 with E-K); row cancellation in F_q[T] at r <= 4 is present for every weight, random non-multiplicative included. Left open: a target-specific treatment. Ceiling 2/3 from row Z24. Round 9 (planner edit, round 10; c9-eh-dual-r5-target-excess, one referee; evidence text corrected against the referee file by c10-repair-record-referee-r9): closed in the model as a source of a target-specific input: the non-principal row sum is a linear functional of the weight with target-independent kernel (proved); the pre-registered target excess over seeded random multiplicative and non-multiplicative classes is not detected at q = 7, r <= 5 (24 seeds per class at r = 5, resolution 0.05 to 0.07 in the exponent). Referee wording: not detected, not absent; power of the test unknown; an excess below 0.05 or setting in at r >= 6 is not excluded; linearity does not imply norm type, the measurement supports it; Lemma A in the model is a sketch for q -> infinity, its number-field sub-step is open. Not a theorem that no proof of (E-H) from the rows exists. Map row Z31

devices.name: Sum rule with positive terms crossing from summable to square-summable coefficients (Szego-Verblunsky, Killip-Simon, Simon-Zlatos) on the prime stub chain
devices.evidence: lane c9-szego-sum-rule-prime-cascade (round 9, one referee holds, eight corrections of scope and wording): closed for five named forms, not for every sum rule (referee E5): Littlewood window functional (Jensen count), mean form (classical density identity), stage functionals continuous in the phases, the Simon-Zlatos type difference condition (a coefficient condition only; no theorem of that family is stated for a product over incommensurable delays), H^2 point evaluation (reaches Re s > sigma_0 + 1/2; Hedenmalm-Lindqvist-Seip). Controls U (torus rotation), THIN (difference condition holds for sigma > b/2 with a zero at b), Liouville twist, WT, FM pass every step; DH and HEAT fail only at chain formation; five controls not run. Not covered: a sum rule whose coefficient side vanishes identically with a semicontinuous limit step (that limit step is the R4 statement). Map row Q27

devices.name: Bridge (spinor square-root) form built from one completed probe row B_m
devices.evidence: closed by c8-single-row-bridge-crossing (round 8, one referee, holds with five wording corrections): a theta row is T = L0 D with L0 = L(3s - 1/2, psi); the row axis Re s = 1/2 is Re w = 1 for L0 (1/6 in s from its own axis), so the bridge of T is blind to zeros of L0; the bridge of D reads them as an identity with no sign; the target enters one row only as a coefficient twist. Kubota-Patterson normalisation in bridge language. Map row Q26

devices.name: Mechanism of the 2026 Landau-Siegel claim (conductor-aspect family of real characters)
devices.evidence: lane c7-landau-siegel-device-read (round 7, one referee; Lean tree read as text, not compiled): interpolation determinant over a box in Z[sqrt d, sqrt 2] with Frobenius-congruence divisibility against the prime bias of a real zero. Floor: real zeros with 1 - beta <= c/log q only; empty to the left; no height-aspect form (n^(-it) is control U). THIN and the Liouville twist fail at S4/S5. The statement itself follows from the compiled Dirichlet 7/8 theorem. State set to closed FOR THE HEIGHT ASPECT by c9-repair-referee-debts-r8 (was floored): the engine target is a height-aspect statement, the lane (referee holds) found no height-aspect form and no crossing outside width c/log q, and the closed outcome record c7-landau-siegel-device-read already rejected every candidate containing the node (1,060). The conductor-aspect statement keeps its floor 1 - c/log q; reopen as floored only with a lane that names a conductor-to-height transfer

devices.name: Reciprocity of twisted second moments exchanging the twist variable with the modulus (Conrey, Young, Bettin; Bettin-Conrey cotangent-sum period relation), as the RS-1 device: functional equation of the target joined to periodicity in the modulus
devices.evidence: lane c11-rs1-twist-modulus-reciprocity (round 11). CLOSED at stage A by c12-repair-sources-statement-o-v3 (round 12) on two referee files: push/c11-rs1-twist-modulus-reciprocity/REFEREE.md (independent; holds with corrections E1 to E6) and push/c12-repair-sources-statement-o-v3/REFEREE2.md section 2 (control table re-derived; Bettin arXiv:1607.05595 opened). The T-NR twin passes every step that holds for zeta with general twists prime to p (nine-term identity, exact at every s) and its bound is false at its zeros in the strip; the window translate passes by substitution; for twist length >= p - 1 and free weights the candidate is its conclusion (zero-one law); the functional equation of the target is not read. Withdrawn: the E_a pass (a linear form, not the candidate), the abscissa claim for short twists, exact reciprocity at height t != 0 (not in the opened source). Map row Z34. Reason for the entry: STRATEGY v3 section 3.1 item 25 names a reciprocity acting on the Moebius variable l as the only reopening input of lead 4 (map row P52). First controls: E_a, T-NR, EIS-w, window translate. Existing partner nodes cotangent-reciprocity-period-function and bettin-conrey-intercept are measured phenomena and are not device nodes

devices.name: Matrix Dirichlet series M_q(s) = sum_n R(n) n^-s over the regular representation of (Z/q)^*, entrywise non-negative, with matrix Euler product and Gauss-sum functional equation; bridge / Krein square for the matrix symbol (RS-1 with the bridge square)
devices.evidence: lane c11-rs1-regular-rep-matrix-bridge (round 11). CLOSED at stage A, for the displayed forms (K), (E), (Q), (H), by c12-repair-sources-statement-o-v3 (round 12) on two referee files: push/c11-rs1-regular-rep-matrix-bridge/REFEREE.md (independent; holds with six corrections) and push/c12-repair-sources-statement-o-v3/REFEREE2.md section 1 (E_a and T-NR lifts re-derived step by step). The bridge objects lie in the commutative group algebra and decompose over characters; the vector 1 is in the cone and is the chi_0 eigenvector, so every cone-quantified statement restricts to the scalar zeta statement (RH for forms K and E); the E_a lift keeps entry positivity at both levels, the Euler product, a functional equation of Gauss-sum type (squared root-number matrix, degree-two gamma factor) and periodicity; the T-NR lift keeps product-level positivity, the Euler product, the functional equation of M_q itself and periodicity. Not covered: a cone other than R_+^G (lane c12-univ-pointwise-control-wcone); statements mixing several bridge objects. Map row Q28. Device type absent from the list before round 11 (no map row for matrix-valued or regular-representation objects). DH at q = 5 is a non-eigen linear functional of M_5. First controls: E_a, T-NR, EIS-w, window translate; bridge rows Q25, Q26 (family sums have gain 0; single rows have their axis at the edge of the Euler factor) are the closed neighbours

devices.name: de Branges positivity condition for Euler products with the gamma factor, and the variants not covered by its known failure for zeta (twin-ladder shift, conductor family), as the RS-3 device
devices.evidence: lane c11-rs3-debranges-positivity-family (round 11). CLOSED at stage A by c12-repair-sources-statement-o-v3 (round 12) on two referee files: push/c11-rs3-debranges-positivity-family/REFEREE.md (independent part; holds with corrections E1 to E4) and push/c12-repair-sources-statement-o-v3/REFEREE2.md section 3 (lattice control re-derived; Bohr 1916 Satz A opened). Every variant examined is a restatement of a closed row (T3, G6) or is false for zeta at a named step: the condition implies a phase balance at every zero, which fails at zero 34 (h = 1) in the entire-function form and next to the first zero in the weight form (measured, not interval-certified); the two-parameter weight family is false for every conclusion half-plane sigma_0 <= 1 relative to Bohr. A lattice passes the hypotheses and necessary conditions. Open cells kept in the evidence: backward heat at the phase-balance step (not run), the tied conductor family (argued only; lane c12-heat-tied-family-open-cell). Map row P53. The condition is reported to fail for zeta (Conrey-Li 2000; relative to that source, not on file). First controls: DH, E_a with real a, backward heat. The node de-branges-hamiltonian-xi is a target form, not a device
